name: Question 11
problem:
Consider the vector field $F=⟨z,\,0,\,x⟩$ and the closed surface $S$ that encloses the finite region between the paraboloid $z=9-{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}$ and the plane $z=1.$ Let $D$ be the projection of $S$ onto the $xy$-plane. The flux of $F$ across $S$ can be expressed in terms of a double integral as 

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS={∬}_{D}\,\,\text{d}A.
$$

Which of the following could be the missing expression?
worked_solution:
Since we have a closed surface, the positive orientation is outward-pointing by convention. So,

- the upper surface ${S}_{1}:z=g(x,y)=9-{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}$ is oriented upward, and

- the lower surface ${S}_{2}:z=h(x,y)=1$ is oriented downward.

Now, we write down the flux across each of the surfaces separately.

- Consider the upper paraboloid ${S}_{1}.$

We compute the partial derivatives of $z=g(x,y):$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂g}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(9-{x}^{2}-{y}^{2})=-2x \\ \frac{∂g}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(9-{x}^{2}-{y}^{2})=-2y\end{aligned}
$$

If we denote $F=⟨P,\,Q,\,R⟩,$ then

$$
P=z=9-{x}^{2}-{y}^{2},\,Q=0,\,R=x.
$$

 

As a result, since the positive orientation is upward, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{{S}_{1}}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}(-P\frac{∂g}{∂x}-Q\frac{∂g}{∂y}+R)\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(-(9-{x}^{2}-{y}^{2})\cdot (-2x)-(0)\cdot (-2y)+x)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(18x-2{x}^{3}-2x{y}^{2}+x)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}19x-2{x}^{3}-2x{y}^{2}\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

- Consider lower plane ${S}_{2}.$ 

Since the positive orientation is downward, the unit normal vector to the plane is $n=⟨0,0,-1⟩.$ As a result, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{{S}_{2}}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{{S}_{2}}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S \\  & ={∬}_{D}⟨z,0,x⟩\cdot ⟨0,0,-1⟩\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}-x\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the flux across the entire surface is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{{S}_{1}}F\cdot \text{d}S+{∬}_{{S}_{2}}F\cdot \text{d}S \\  & ={∬}_{D}19x-2{x}^{3}-2x{y}^{2}\,\text{d}A+{∬}_{D}-x\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}18x-2{x}^{3}-2x{y}^{2}\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 11
?

Consider the vector field F=⟨z,0,x⟩ and the closed surface S that encloses the finite region between the paraboloid z=9−x2−y2 and the plane z=1. Let D be the projection of S onto the xy-plane. The flux of F across S can be expressed in terms of a double integral as ∬SF⋅dS=∬DAAAAAAAdA. Which of the following could be the missing expression?

a
 19x−2x3+3y2
b
 20x+x3−2xy2
c
18x−2x3−2xy2
d
 16x−xy2+2y2
e
 20x+2yx3−2xy2
Don't Know
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Since we have a closed surface, the positive orientation is outward-pointing by convention. So,

  • the upper surface S1:z=g(x,y)=9−x2−y2 is oriented upward, and

  • the lower surface S2:z=h(x,y)=1 is oriented downward.

Now, we write down the flux across each of the surfaces separately.

  • Consider the upper paraboloid S1.

    We compute the partial derivatives of z=g(x,y): ∂g∂x=∂∂x(9−x2−y2)=−2x∂g∂y=∂∂y(9−x2−y2)=−2y

    If we denote F=⟨P,Q,R⟩, then P=z=9−x2−y2,Q=0,R=x.

    As a result, since the positive orientation is upward, we have ∬S1F⋅dS=∬D(−P∂g∂x−Q∂g∂y+R)dA=∬D(−(9−x2−y2)⋅(−2x)−(0)⋅(−2y)+x)dA=∬D(18x−2x3−2xy2+x)dA=∬D19x−2x3−2xy2dA.

  • Consider lower plane S2.

    Since the positive orientation is downward, the unit normal vector to the plane is n=⟨0,0,−1⟩. As a result, we have ∬S2F⋅dS=∬S2F⋅ndS=∬D⟨z,0,x⟩⋅⟨0,0,−1⟩dA=∬D−xdA.

Therefore, the flux across the entire surface is

∬SF⋅dS=∬S1F⋅dS+∬S2F⋅dS=∬D19x−2x3−2xy2dA+∬D−xdA=∬D18x−2x3−2xy2dA.
